div.head: VI Atr 29
div.ab: K. ⁊ la understande man georne, þæt eal swylc is to leanne ⁊ næfre to lufianne.
⁊ la understande man georne þæt eal swylc is to leanne ⁊ næfre to lufianne.
And la, understande man georne þæt ealswylc is to leanne and næfre to lufianne.
Und traun, man begreife ernstlich, dass all solches zu verschmähen und niemals zu pflegen ist.
And indeed, let it be earnestly understood that all such things are to be rejected and never cherished.
And now behold it must be clearly understood that all such are to be censured and not to be indulged in.
And indeed it is to be wholly understood that all such sins are to be condemned and never to be admired.

note.seg: understande man ist häufig in Homil. n. Wulfstan 161f.; vgl. I Cn 1b D. 4, 1. 26.—Die alliterirenden lean ⁊ lufian nebeneinander zitiert aus Prosa 11. Jhs. Toller s. v. leán
understande man is frequent in Homil. n. Wulfstan 161f.; cf. I Cn 1b D. 4, 1. 26.—Toller s. v. leán cites the alliterating lean ⁊ lufian side by side from 11th-cent. prose
This clause is not found in V Atr.
This phrase is of frequent occurrence in Wulfstan’s sermons.
